payload.name: Preserve all explicit evaluative phrases in extraction
payload.description: When extracting an event memory from a message where a speaker states an overall evaluation and then adds supporting qualities, include both the overall evaluation and the supporting qualities in the candidate content.
content: During candidate extraction from a message containing an explicit overall evaluation plus supporting details, record both the overall evaluation and the supporting qualities in the memory content.
Do not keep only the first-listed or most concrete attribute; preserve each explicit evaluative phrase that could answer a future question about the speaker's opinion.
When a single message has multiple distinct evaluative terms about the same subject, include all of them in a compact paraphrase.

solves: Extraction often drops an explicit summary sentiment when a single message also contains supporting qualities, leaving memory unable to answer later questions about the full opinion. This rule applies during construction extraction whenever one message has multiple distinct explicit evaluative phrases about the same subject; keep all of them in the candidate content. It does not apply to inferring unstated sentiment.
